title: Case study: the Jurua River (Acre, Brazil)
text: Start giving file diagnose(): Note rsguide worked : Sensor: band names (B02, B03, …, B12), image Sentinel-2. band matched spectral region (blue, green, red, infrared…). Scale: values integers almost 1000. reveals +1000 offset Sentinel-2 introduced 2022: actual reflectance (value - 1000) / 10000. Forgetting detail common mistake distorts indices EVI. Suggestions: blue, green, red, red edge, near shortwave infrared, image supports vegetation, water burn indices, well land cover classification. read rationale caveats analysis, use summary(). keep document short, beginning shown :
code: img <- file.path(folder, "jurua_s2_20240814.tif") d <- diagnose(img) d #> ══ rsguide diagnosis ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ #> Inputs: 1 raster #>  #> ── R1 · jurua_s2_20240814 (raster) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> • Layers: 7 | Dimensions: 250 rows × 250 columns | Resolution: 10 m #> • CRS: WGS 84 / UTM zone 18S (EPSG:32718) #> • Extent: x from 757,564 to 760,064; y from 9,152,550 to 9,155,050 #> • Likely sensor: Sentinel-2 (MSI) (high confidence) #> • Bands: B02 = blue; B03 = green; B04 = red; B05 = red edge; B08 = near infrared; B11 = shortwave infrared 1; B12 = shortwave infrared 2 #> • Value scale: scaled integers with offset (reflectance = (value - 1000) / 10,000) #> • Values: minimum 920, maximum 14,192 #> • NA (no data): 0.0% in the layer with most NA #> • Date(s): 2024-08-14 (file name) #>  #> ── Alerts ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> i [R1] Almost all values are above 1000: the image seems to carry the +1000 offset of Sentinel-2 L2A (processing since 2022-01-25, including the reprocessed Collection 1). Convert to reflectance with (r - 1000) / 10000 before computing indices. #>  #> ══ Suggested analyses (10) ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ #> Vegetation indices #>   • NDVI (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index) [ndvi] → 'jurua_s2_20240814' #>   • EVI (Enhanced Vegetation Index) [evi] → 'jurua_s2_20240814' #>   • SAVI (Soil-Adjusted Vegetation Index) [savi] → 'jurua_s2_20240814' #>   • NDRE (Normalized Difference Red Edge index) [ndre] → 'jurua_s2_20240814' #>   • NDMI (Normalized Difference Moisture Index) [ndmi] → 'jurua_s2_20240814' #> Water #>   • NDWI (Normalized Difference Water Index, McFeeters) [ndwi] → 'jurua_s2_20240814' #>   • MNDWI (Modified NDWI) [mndwi] → 'jurua_s2_20240814' #> Fire #>   • NBR (Normalized Burn Ratio) and dNBR [nbr] → 'jurua_s2_20240814' #> Classification #>   • Supervised land use and land cover classification [supervised_class] → 'jurua_s2_20240814' #>   • Unsupervised classification (clustering) [unsupervised_class] → 'jurua_s2_20240814' #>  #> i Rationale and caveats: summary(). Example code: show_code(..., "ndvi"). Table to export: as.data.frame(). overview <- capture.output(summary(d)) cat(head(overview, 30), sep = "\n") #> ══ rsguide diagnosis summary ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ #> R1   jurua_s2_20240814 (raster)  #>      7 layers · 10 m · EPSG:32718 · Sentinel-2 (MSI) · scaled integers with offset #>        (reflectance = (value - 1000) / 10,000) · 2024-08-14 #> Alerts: 0 warning(s) and 1 note(s); see print() or as.data.frame(..., type = "alerts"). #>  #> ══ Suggested analyses (10) ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ #>  #> Vegetation indices #> 1. NDVI (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index) [ndvi] #>    Applies to: 'jurua_s2_20240814' #>    Why: Healthy vegetation strongly reflects near infrared and absorbs red light. NDVI #>      uses this contrast to indicate how much green vegetation each pixel contains #>      (values from -1 to 1). #>    Caveats: #>      - Use surface reflectance (atmospherically corrected imagery, level L2A/L2) #>      - Mask clouds and shadows first #>      - In dense forests, such as the Amazon, NDVI saturates: it stays close to 1 and #>        stops discriminating; consider EVI #>    Packages: terra #> 2. EVI (Enhanced Vegetation Index) [evi] #>    Applies to: 'jurua_s2_20240814' #>    Why: Similar to NDVI, but also uses the blue band to reduce atmospheric and soil #>      effects. It saturates less in dense vegetation, which makes it popular in tropical #>      forests. #>    Caveats: #>      - The formula only works with reflectance on a 0-1 scale: convert the values first #>      - Mask clouds and shadows #>      - Values far outside -1 to 1 point to scale problems or clouds #>    Packages: terra

text: suggestion comes example code already filled path file, names bands right scale conversion. code MNDWI, index highlights water: code can copied run . run straight text returned show_code():  main channel Jurua shows corners image horseshoe-shaped meander crosses center. water threshold (mndwi > 0) starting point: caveats say, checked image.
code: code <- show_code(d, "mndwi") #> ── MNDWI (Modified NDWI) - 'jurua_s2_20240814' ─────────────────────────────────────────── #> # MNDWI = (green - SWIR1) / (green + SWIR1) #> img <- terra::rast("/home/runner/work/_temp/Library/rsguide/extdata/jurua_s2_20240814.tif") #> img <- (img - 1000) / 10000  # removes the offset and converts to 0-1 reflectance #> mndwi <- (img[["B03"]] - img[["B11"]]) / (img[["B03"]] + img[["B11"]]) #> names(mndwi) <- "MNDWI" #> terra::plot(mndwi, main = "MNDWI") #> water <- mndwi > 0  # starting threshold; adjust it by looking at the image #> terra::plot(water, main = "Water (MNDWI > 0)") eval(parse(text = code))

title: Case study: the Jurua River (Acre, Brazil)
text: code suggested time series computes NDVI difference first last dates:  Positive values (vegetation gain) appear along banks meander, seem colonized vegetation. negative values, contrast, main river channel (bottom-left corner): vegetation loss , change water (color, sediment, river level), also affects NDVI. every “change” vegetation! interpret safely, compare true-color images keep caveats mind: season, scale clouds either date.
code: show_code(dd, "change_detection") #> ── Change detection between dates - time series with 2 dates ───────────────────────────── #> # Change detection: difference in NDVI between the first and last dates #> imgs <- list(  # in date order #>   terra::rast("/home/runner/work/_temp/Library/rsguide/extdata/jurua_s2_20190816.tif"), #>   terra::rast("/home/runner/work/_temp/Library/rsguide/extdata/jurua_s2_20240814.tif") #> ) #> dates <- as.Date(c("2019-08-16", "2024-08-14")) #> convert <- function(x) (x - 1000) / 10000 #> index <- function(x) (x[["B08"]] - x[["B04"]]) / (x[["B08"]] + x[["B04"]]) #> before <- index(convert(imgs[[1]])) #> after <- index(convert(imgs[[length(imgs)]])) #> if (!terra::compareGeom(before, after, stopOnError = FALSE)) after <- terra::resample(after, before) #> change <- after - before #> terra::plot(change, main = paste("NDVI:", dates[length(dates)], "minus", dates[1])) #> # Strongly negative values indicate loss (e.g. deforestation); positive values, gain eval(parse(text = show_code(dd, "change_detection")))

code: folder <- system.file("extdata", package = "rsguide") d <- diagnose(folder)  for (cx in d$contexts) {   cat(cx$id, "-", cx$label, "\n  ", paste(cx$tags, collapse = ", "), "\n") } #> SC1 - 'jurua_dem_copernicus'  #>    raster, scale:elevation, dem  #> SC2 - 'jurua_s2_20190816'  #>    raster, band:blue, band:green, band:red, band:rededge, band:nir, band:swir1, band:swir2, scale:int_10000, multispectral  #> SC3 - 'jurua_s2_20240814'  #>    raster, band:blue, band:green, band:red, band:rededge, band:nir, band:swir1, band:swir2, scale:int_10000, multispectral  #> S1 - time series with 2 dates  #>    raster, time_series, band:blue, band:green, band:red, band:rededge, band:nir, band:swir1, band:swir2, multispectral  #> T1 - 'jurua_plots'  #>    vector, vector:points, table  #> SC1+T1 - 'jurua_dem_copernicus' + 'jurua_plots'  #>    raster, scale:elevation, dem, vector, vector:points, table, overlap, crs_mismatch  #> SC2+T1 - 'jurua_s2_20190816' + 'jurua_plots'  #>    raster, band:blue, band:green, band:red, band:rededge, band:nir, band:swir1, band:swir2, scale:int_10000, multispectral, vector, vector:points, table, overlap, crs_mismatch  #> SC3+T1 - 'jurua_s2_20240814' + 'jurua_plots'  #>    raster, band:blue, band:green, band:red, band:rededge, band:nir, band:swir1, band:swir2, scale:int_10000, multispectral, vector, vector:points, table, overlap, crs_mismatch

It is more sensitive to chlorophyll",     "concentration and saturates less than NDVI in dense vegetation."   ),   caveats = "Use surface reflectance | Mask clouds and shadows",   packages = "terra" ) my_rules <- rbind(rules, gndvi)  img <- file.path(folder, "jurua_s2_20240814.tif") d <- diagnose(img, rules = my_rules) d$suggestions[d$suggestions$id == "gndvi", c("analysis", "applies_to")] #>              analysis          applies_to #> 11 GNDVI (Green NDVI) 'jurua_s2_20240814'

title: Writing your own rules
text: Without template analysis still suggested, show_code() nothing show. template regular .R file placeholders braces, rsguide replaces user’s data: NDVI template, example: Let’s write GNDVI template point template column: Note rsguide already added (img - 1000) / 10000 conversion, detected Sentinel-2 offset image.
code: cat(readLines(system.file("templates", "ndvi.R", package = "rsguide")), sep = "\n") #> # NDVI = (NIR - red) / (NIR + red) #> {load_raster:img} #> {scale} #> ndvi <- (img[["{nir}"]] - img[["{red}"]]) / (img[["{nir}"]] + img[["{red}"]]) #> names(ndvi) <- "NDVI" #> terra::plot(ndvi, main = "NDVI") #> # terra::writeRaster(ndvi, "ndvi.tif") template <- tempfile(fileext = ".R")  # use a path of yours, e.g. "templates/gndvi.R" writeLines(c(   "# GNDVI = (NIR - green) / (NIR + green)",   "{load_raster:img}",   "{scale}",   "gndvi <- (img[[\"{nir}\"]] - img[[\"{green}\"]]) / (img[[\"{nir}\"]] + img[[\"{green}\"]])",   "terra::plot(gndvi, main = \"GNDVI\")" ), template)  gndvi$template <- template rules$template <- NA d <- diagnose(img, rules = rbind(rules, gndvi)) show_code(d, "gndvi") #> ── GNDVI (Green NDVI) - 'jurua_s2_20240814' ────────────────────────────────────────────── #> # GNDVI = (NIR - green) / (NIR + green) #> img <- terra::rast("/home/runner/work/_temp/Library/rsguide/extdata/jurua_s2_20240814.tif") #> img <- (img - 1000) / 10000  # removes the offset and converts to 0-1 reflectance #> gndvi <- (img[["B08"]] - img[["B03"]]) / (img[["B08"]] + img[["B03"]]) #> terra::plot(gndvi, main = "GNDVI")

title: Diagnose Remote Sensing Data and Suggest Analyses
text: diagnose() identifies: type data: raster, vector (points, lines, polygons) table coordinates (lon/lat, x/y, decimalLongitude/decimalLatitude…); layers, resolution, coordinate reference system, extent missing values; bands likely sensor (Sentinel-2, Landsat 4-9 generic names red, nir, swir1); value scale (0-1 reflectance, integers x 10,000, Landsat Collection 2, +1000 offset Sentinel-2…); digital elevation models, class maps time series; whether vectors fall raster, whether coordinate systems match. Analyses can suggested: NDVI, EVI, SAVI, NDRE, NDMI, NDWI, MNDWI, NBR, supervised unsupervised classification, change detection, trend analysis, slope, aspect, watersheds drainage, extraction values points, zonal statistics landscape metrics.
code: library(rsguide)  # A file, an R object or a whole folder folder <- system.file("extdata", package = "rsguide") d <- diagnose(folder) d                     # diagnosis and list of suggested analyses summary(d)            # rationale and caveats of each analysis show_code(d, "ndvi")  # code ready to copy as.data.frame(d)      # report as a table (to save as CSV)

title: Diagnose remote sensing data — diagnose
code: r <- terra::rast(nrows = 20, ncols = 20, nlyrs = 4, crs = "EPSG:32718",                  extent = terra::ext(500000, 500200, 9150000, 9150200)) terra::values(r) <- round(runif(terra::ncell(r) * 4, 100, 4000)) names(r) <- c("B2", "B3", "B4", "B8") diagnose(r) #> ══ rsguide diagnosis ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ #> Inputs: 1 raster #>  #> ── R1 · r (raster) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> • Layers: 4 | Dimensions: 20 rows × 20 columns | Resolution: 10 m #> • CRS: WGS 84 / UTM zone 18S (EPSG:32718) #> • Extent: x from 500,000 to 500,200; y from 9,150,000 to 9,150,200 #> • Likely sensor: Sentinel-2 (MSI) (low confidence) #> • Bands: B2 = blue; B3 = green; B4 = red; B8 = near infrared #> • Value scale: scaled integers (reflectance x 10,000) #> • Values: minimum 100, maximum 3,999 #> • NA (no data): 0.0% in the layer with most NA #>  #> ── Alerts ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ! [R1] The band names match more than one sensor (Sentinel-2 (MSI), Landsat 8/9 (OLI/TIRS)). I assumed Sentinel-2 (MSI); if that is wrong, use diagnose(..., sensor = "landsat89"). #> i [R1] Values look like reflectance x 10,000. For indices such as EVI and SAVI, convert first: r / 10000. Note: Sentinel-2 L2A images processed since 2022-01-25 have a -1000 offset [reflectance = (value - 1000) / 10000]; some providers already remove it, check yours. #>  #> ══ Suggested analyses (6) ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ #> Vegetation indices #>   • NDVI (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index) [ndvi] → 'r' #>   • EVI (Enhanced Vegetation Index) [evi] → 'r' #>   • SAVI (Soil-Adjusted Vegetation Index) [savi] → 'r' #> Water #>   • NDWI (Normalized Difference Water Index, McFeeters) [ndwi] → 'r' #> Classification #>   • Supervised land use and land cover classification [supervised_class] → 'r' #>   • Unsupervised classification (clustering) [unsupervised_class] → 'r' #>  #> i Rationale and caveats: summary(). Example code: show_code(..., "ndvi"). Table to export: as.data.frame().

title: Summarize and export a diagnosis — diagnosis-summary
code: r <- terra::rast(nrows = 20, ncols = 20, nlyrs = 4, crs = "EPSG:32718",                  extent = terra::ext(500000, 500200, 9150000, 9150200)) terra::values(r) <- round(runif(terra::ncell(r) * 4, 100, 4000)) names(r) <- c("B2", "B3", "B4", "B8") d <- diagnose(r) summary(d) #> ══ rsguide diagnosis summary ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════ #> R1   r (raster)  #>      4 layers · 10 m · EPSG:32718 · Sentinel-2 (MSI) · scaled integers #>        (reflectance x 10,000) #> Alerts: 1 warning(s) and 1 note(s); see print() or as.data.frame(..., type = "alerts"). #>  #> ══ Suggested analyses (6) ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ #>  #> Vegetation indices #> 1. NDVI (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index) [ndvi] #>    Applies to: 'r' #>    Why: Healthy vegetation strongly reflects near infrared and absorbs red #>      light. NDVI uses this contrast to indicate how much green vegetation #>      each pixel contains (values from -1 to 1). #>    Caveats: #>      - Use surface reflectance (atmospherically corrected imagery, level #>        L2A/L2) #>      - Mask clouds and shadows first #>      - In dense forests, such as the Amazon, NDVI saturates: it stays close #>        to 1 and stops discriminating; consider EVI #>    Packages: terra #> 2. EVI (Enhanced Vegetation Index) [evi] #>    Applies to: 'r' #>    Why: Similar to NDVI, but also uses the blue band to reduce atmospheric #>      and soil effects. It saturates less in dense vegetation, which makes it #>      popular in tropical forests. #>    Caveats: #>      - The formula only works with reflectance on a 0-1 scale: convert the #>        values first #>      - Mask clouds and shadows #>      - Values far outside -1 to 1 point to scale problems or clouds #>    Packages: terra #> 3. SAVI (Soil-Adjusted Vegetation Index) [savi] #>    Applies to: 'r' #>    Why: A version of NDVI that reduces the influence of bare soil. #>      Recommended where vegetation is sparse: degraded pastures, regenerating #>      areas, grasslands and open savannas. #>    Caveats: #>      - The L factor (0.5 is the default) changes the result; use the same L #>        for all images #>      - Requires reflectance on a 0-1 scale #>      - Mask clouds and shadows #>    Packages: terra #>  #> Water #> 4. NDWI (Normalized Difference Water Index, McFeeters) [ndwi] #>    Applies to: 'r' #>    Why: Water reflects green light and absorbs almost all near infrared. NDWI #>      highlights rivers, lakes and flooded areas; positive values usually #>      indicate water. #>    Caveats: #>      - Built-up areas and bare soil can also have high values; MNDWI #>        separates them better #>      - The water/non-water threshold (e.g. 0) varies between scenes: check it #>        on the image #>      - Sediment-laden rivers (such as the Jurua) reflect more and may get #>        lower values #>    Packages: terra #>  #> Classification #> 5. Supervised land use and land cover classification [supervised_class] #>    Applies to: 'r' #>    Why: With several bands, each cover type (forest, pasture, water, urban) #>      has its own spectral signature. You provide examples of each class and #>      an algorithm (e.g. Random Forest) classifies the rest of the image. #>    Caveats: #>      - Requires labeled training samples (points or polygons for each class) #>      - Validate with independent samples (confusion matrix, accuracy) #>      - Mask clouds and use images from the same date or season #>    Packages: terra; sf; randomForest #> 6. Unsupervised classification (clustering) [unsupervised_class] #>    Applies to: 'r' #>    Why: The algorithm (e.g. k-means) groups similar pixels without training #>      samples. It is a good first exploration of the landscape. #>    Caveats: #>      - Clusters have no names: you interpret what each one represents #>      - The number of clusters is your choice; try a few values #>      - Clouds and shadows form their own clusters #>    Packages: terra #>  #> i To see the code: show_code(..., "ndvi") or summary(..., code = TRUE). report <- as.data.frame(d) report[, c("analysis", "packages")] #>                                              analysis                packages #> 1       NDVI (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index)                   terra #> 2                     EVI (Enhanced Vegetation Index)                   terra #> 3               SAVI (Soil-Adjusted Vegetation Index)                   terra #> 4 NDWI (Normalized Difference Water Index, McFeeters)                   terra #> 5   Supervised land use and land cover classification terra; sf; randomForest #> 6            Unsupervised classification (clustering)                   terra as.data.frame(d, type = "items") #>   id name   type source layers features geometry resolution_m #> 1 R1    r raster   <NA>      4       NA     <NA>           10 #>                                  crs  epsg           sensor sensor_confidence #> 1 WGS 84 / UTM zone 18S (EPSG:32718) 32718 Sentinel-2 (MSI)               low #>                               bands     scale   dem dates max_prop_na #> 1 B2=blue; B3=green; B4=red; B8=nir int_10000 FALSE  <NA>           0 #>                                                                                description #> 1 4 layers · 10 m · EPSG:32718 · Sentinel-2 (MSI) · scaled integers (reflectance x 10,000)  # Saving the report as CSV (here to a temporary file) file <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv") utils::write.csv(report, file, row.names = FALSE) unlink(file)

title: Recommendation rules — rsguide_rules
text: Required columns: id: short, unique identifier (e.g. "ndvi"). analysis' code template looked inst/templates/<id>.R; custom rules can point another file optional column template. analysis, category: name analysis group belongs . condition: expression using tags produced diagnose(), combined & (), | () ! (). Example: "band:green & band:nir | band:green & band:swir1". rationale: analysis possible data. caveats: assumptions precautions, separated |. packages: suggested R packages, separated ;. Available tags: raster, vector, table, multispectral, dem, time_series, long_series, overlap, crs_mismatch, band:<group> (coastal, blue, green, red, rededge, nir, swir1, swir2, thermal, quality), scale:<type> (reflectance_0_1, int_10000, landsat_c2, int_8bit, index, categorical, elevation, unknown) vector:<type> (points, lines, polygons, labeled).

title: rsguide 0.1.0
text: First release. diagnose() identifies rasters, vectors tables coordinates; recognizes bands sensor (Sentinel-2, Landsat 4-9, generic names), value scale (including +1000 offset Sentinel-2), DEMs, class maps, time series raster/vector overlap. suggest_analyses() matches diagnosis editable table 19 rules (rsguide_rules()) suggests analyses rationale, caveats, packages example code already filled (show_code()). print(), summary() .data.frame() read export report.
